proposals.subtype: Abstract base models with protected first constructors
proposals.explanation: The script applies updateModelClassModifierToAbstract to NotificationContent, MessageTemplateValue, MessageTemplateItem, MessageContent and ActionBindings, requesting public abstract class modifiers and protected visibility for each first constructor.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: MessagesSdkCustomization extends Customization and explicitly changes model AST modifiers; these are customization operations, not an inference from an unannotated generated model.

proposals.subtype: Replace known-discriminator fallback with an exception
proposals.explanation: For the five models passed through updateModelClassModifierToAbstract, removeJsonKnownDiscriminatorMethod requests a literal replacement of return fromJsonKnownDiscriminator(readerToUse.reset()) with an IllegalStateException containing discriminatorValue, and removes methods named fromJsonKnownDiscriminator. This describes the scripted fallback edit, not a verified deserialization outcome.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The customization helper rewrites fromJson method bodies and removes a named generated fallback through customizeAst.

proposals.subtype: Connection-string builder API and bearer-or-HMAC policy wiring
proposals.explanation: For NotificationMessagesClientBuilder and MessageTemplateClientBuilder, updateBuilderClass adds missing token/key/connection-string traits, adds a connectionString method that extracts a key and endpoint, and adds an auth-policy factory that prefers token credentials, otherwise constructs an imported HMAC policy from the key, otherwise throws. It replaces pipeline construction to include date and auth policies after the retry policy while retaining configured policy positions. Captured builder excerpts corroborate both connection-string methods and both auth factories; the imported authentication algorithms are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A Customization subclass explicitly adds these members and replaces createHttpPipeline. The corresponding concrete builder snippets match the scripted connection-string and auth-selection behavior.

proposals.subtype: Register and use an internal model-name setter bridge
proposals.explanation: The script adds a MessageTemplateItem static initializer that registers MessageTemplateItem::setName in MessageTemplateItemAccessHelper, then requests that WhatsAppMessageTemplateItem.fromJson use the helper instead of directly invoking setName. The captured helper stores an accessor and delegates setName through it. These linked pieces are one internal-access bridge; the commented-out BinaryData getter edit is not active behavior.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The customization script explicitly installs and calls the bridge, connecting the otherwise unknown-provenance access-helper implementation to a targeted generated-model edit.

proposals.subtype: GeoPosition constructor and accessor replace scalar coordinate APIs
proposals.explanation: customizeMessageTemplateLocation makes existing constructors private, adds a public (String refValue, GeoPosition geoPosition) constructor that forwards refValue and copies latitude/longitude, removes scalar coordinate getters and adds getPosition returning new GeoPosition(longitude, latitude). Captured constructor and getter excerpts corroborate the richer coordinate-object API.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The script explicitly changes constructor visibility, adds the adapter constructor/getter and removes named scalar getters; corresponding concrete model excerpts are supplied.

proposals.explanation: customizeInteractiveMessage renames getHeaderProperty/setHeaderProperty to getHeader/setHeader, changes the setter parameter and body to use header, and requests related Javadoc replacements. Captured getHeader and setHeader methods continue to read/write the underlying headerProperty field.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The customization script names and rewrites the generated accessors, and the supplied model fragments contain the resulting accessor names and field access.

proposals.subtype: Deprecate a model class and normalize its deprecation documentation
proposals.explanation: addDeprecateAnnotationToMediaNotificationContent requests an @Deprecated marker on MediaNotificationContent and replaces the escaped @deprecated text in the first Javadoc description element with @deprecated when documentation is present.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Customization subclass explicitly adds the annotation and edits the model's Javadoc AST.

proposals.explanation: addDeprecateAnnotationForImageV0CommunicationKind finds CommunicationMessageKind.IMAGE_V0, adds @Deprecated and, when present, changes its Javadoc by replacing Image message type. with @deprecated.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The script explicitly targets a field and changes its annotation and documentation through customizeAst.

proposals.explanation: For ActionBindings and MessageContent, updateJavaDocForMethodFromJson requests replacement of the existing IOException throws text with an IllegalStateException description for missing required properties followed by the original IOException text. This is a documentation edit, not independent evidence of additional runtime validation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A customization helper explicitly calls setJavadocComment on selected fromJson methods.

proposals.subtype: Shallow list copies in a model constructor and getter
proposals.explanation: customizeActionGroup requests replacing direct assignment of items with new ArrayList<>(items) in the (String, List) constructor and replacing return this.items with return new ArrayList<>(this.items) in getItems. These are shallow collection copies, not deep copies or a demonstrated null-handling change.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The script explicitly replaces constructor and getter body text on ActionGroup.

proposals.explanation: customizeActionGroupContent requests new ArrayList<>(groups) instead of direct groups assignment in the (String, List) constructor and new ArrayList<>(this.groups) instead of returning the stored list from getGroups.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A named customization helper edits ActionGroupContent constructor and getter bodies.

proposals.handwrittenRationale: The customization script replaces the selected ButtonSetContent constructor and getter body text.

decisions.reason: The handwritten Customization subclass invokes this helper on five named models and explicitly requests abstract class and protected first-constructor modifiers. The proposal describes the scripted edit rather than asserting that every target was successfully changed.

Lines 239-247 explicitly request a literal fromJson fallback replacement and remove the named discriminator helper in the five models selected by lines 34-42 and 65. Serialization is appropriate; the wording correctly does not claim that the replacement matched or prove a runtime exception.

The handwritten builder helper adds credential traits and the connection-string method, constructs bearer-or-HMAC authentication, and wires its factory and date policy into the replaced pipeline for both builders. The captured builder excerpts corroborate the two added methods, not the full pipeline or imported policy internals. These linked edits form one credential-configuration/wiring behavior.

Two explicit edits register MessageTemplateItem::setName and rewrite the WhatsApp subtype's fromJson invocation to use the bridge; the supplied helper shows how setAccessor and setName delegate. The helper's independent provenance is unknown, but its integration is demonstrably scripted. The commented BinaryData edit is not counted.

The customization explicitly hides existing constructors, adds the GeoPosition constructor, removes scalar getters and adds getPosition. The two model excerpts corroborate the new constructor and getter, without establishing the absent getters independently; the proposal confines those claims to requested AST operations.

The handwritten script renames both accessors, changes the setter parameter/body, and attempts Javadoc rewrites. The supplied resulting methods access headerProperty under the new names. The proposal does not rely on the Javadoc rewrites succeeding; the getter excerpt still contains the old documentation.

The Customization subclass explicitly adds @Deprecated to MediaNotificationContent and conditionally rewrites its first Javadoc description element. This is a targeted public-model annotation/documentation edit, not a claim that the final model was captured.

The script targets CommunicationMessageKind.IMAGE_V0, requests a deprecation annotation and conditionally changes its Javadoc. Its field lookup is conditional, so this confirms the handwritten edit intent rather than independently proving final annotation state.

The script selects ActionBindings and MessageContent and calls setJavadocComment on fromJson methods after requesting a specific throws-text substitution. Java guidance includes Javadoc customization; the proposal correctly treats this as documentation only, not evidence of additional runtime validation.

Lines 282-290 request shallow list copies on both ingress through the ActionGroup constructor and egress through getItems. The body-text replacements are conditional on matching generated text; the proposal does not claim deep copying or verified runtime behavior.

Lines 292-300 explicitly request constructor and getter body rewrites that copy the ActionGroupContent groups list. This is the same reusable defensive-copy shape as the neighboring model but a distinct model/symbol identity.

Lines 302-309 explicitly request shallow copies of the ButtonSetContent buttons list in its constructor and getter. It is a distinct target model, and the description does not claim the string substitutions were verified in the output.
